conclusion: The attempted schema/registration/compiler rebuttal does not disprove the conditional author-data premise. The simple uppercase-underscore value survives the actual string parsing and move validation path, and registration retains it. The fixed construction path distinguishes an absent named binding from an existing resolved value without construction capability. However the present R5 vectors are expressly absent-name fixtures, so this is not a failure of those vectors or of default401/default740 content. The formal absence wording can reasonably be read as excluding an existing named value, making an observation/clarification recommendation safer than automatically assigning a MEDIUM defect.

formal_scope_analysis.absence_interpretation: WP43 line31 is conditioned on not finding the effect implementation, and line35 plus catalog235 explicitly use the absent ReviewMissingEffect identity. A narrow reference-lookup reading treats an existing named value as outside that absence premise. The vectors therefore remain correct under that reading.
formal_scope_analysis.possible_clarification: The body does not explicitly define whether “implementation not found” means no named binding versus no constructible behavior. An independent implementation reader could regard a resolved nonconstructible value as “no effect implementation” and expect fallback. Clarifying the distinction would avoid this ambiguity while preserving architecture neutrality.
formal_scope_analysis.recommendation: Retain the source behavior as a conditional author-data boundary observation, or accept a small compatibility clarification if root considers line31 to quantify over all valid registered codes without constructible behavior. Do not label it default corruption, a demonstrated runtime crash, or a broken R5 absent-name regression.
